question: What if you couldn't stop growing as a human?

steps.role: Imagine… it happens + what that means
lines: Imagine your body starts growing at its first-year rate again.
Twenty-five centimetres a year, and it never slows.
You are standing in the square of an old canal town.
Today you stand one point eight metres tall.
At twenty-five centimetres a year, eight years add two metres.
The first thing you notice is your shoes.
Tight in spring, split open by autumn.

steps.role: How people react; things in the street
lines: People move back and look up at you.
A cart comes up to your thigh.

steps.role: One real fact with a number
lines: The tallest person ever measured reached two point seven two metres.
He weighed almost two hundred kilos.
You can no longer get through your own door.
You sleep in the square, beside the fountain.
Everything in you grew in proportion, so your weight rose nine times.
But the bone that carries it grew only four times stronger.
Eight years on, your legs carry about twice the load they were built for.
Your head is above the lanterns now.
The square is the only room that fits you.
The market goes on around your legs.
Nothing in a human body was built to be this big.
And the growth has not stopped.

facts.claim: Babies grow about 25 cm in their first year
facts.source: Merck Manual Professional, Physical Growth of Infants and Children
facts.source_says: Infants grow about 25 cm during the first year, and height at 5 years is about double the birth length

facts.source: Guinness World Records, Tallest man ever (Robert Wadlow)
facts.source_says: when last measured on 27 June 1940, was found to be 2.72 m (8 ft 11 in)

facts.claim: That man weighed 199 kg at 2.72 m
facts.source: Guinness World Records, Tallest man ever (Robert Wadlow)
facts.source_says: he weighed 199 kg (31 st 5 lb) at the time of his death

climax.why_it_fits_the_closing_line: The closing line says nothing in a human body was built to be this big, so the climax is not a fall or a break: it is the quiet image of a body standing still in a space built for people half its height, with the market carrying on around it - and the line that the growth itself has not stopped.

models.name: Mini characters (you and the people around you)

derivations.explain: At 25 cm (0.25 m) a year, eight years add 8 x 0.25 = 2 m of height.
1.8 m today plus the 2 m you add in eight years gives 3.8 m - the first line of the counter.
A body 2.11 times taller, keeping its shape, holds 2.11 cubed = 9.4 times as much flesh, so the weight rises nine times.
The cross-section of a bone grows as the square of height, so at 2.11 times the height the bone is only 2.11 squared = 4.4 times stronger.
75 kg times the ninefold rise in weight (9.4) gives about 705 kg - the second line of the counter.
Weight rises 9.4 times but the bone only 4.4 times, so every square centimetre of bone carries 9.4 / 4.4 = 2.1 times the load: about twice.

reality.why_it_really_happens: Real doors are about two metres high, so a body past three metres cannot use an ordinary house at all: the open square becomes the only room in town that fits you, which is why you end up living and sleeping there.

Everything in this scenario keeps its shape, so weight grows as the cube of height while bone cross-section grows as the square: every square centimetre of bone carries 2.1 times the load and every joint twice the pressure, the muscles must move nine times the mass with only four times the strength, and the heart must lift blood more than twice as high as it does now to reach the brain. Food rises more slowly than weight, because metabolism follows mass to the power 0.75: 9.4 times the mass is only about five times the food, roughly thirteen thousand kilocalories a day. Standing still is all that is left; walking ends first. Real giants come out thinner than this sum, because a real body does not keep its shape: the tallest man ever measured weighed 199 kg at 2.72 m, where the growing cube would give 258 kg.

Nothing in the scenario ever closes the growth plates, so no signal turns the growth down: the body stays and keeps adding. The counter measures only the first eight years of that, which is why the closing line says the growth has not stopped.

critic.weak_point: The first draft of step 1 said the growth of your first year never slowed, which would have made you 5 m tall by now - it fought step 3 ('today you stand 1.8 m')
critic.fix: step 1 now starts the change today: your body grows at its first-year rate again, and 25 cm a year never slows

critic.weak_point: The first draft grew you to 5.45 m in one year at an invented rate of one centimetre a day, and at that size no human frame stands
critic.fix: the real fastest rate (about 25 cm in the first year, Merck Manual) over eight years: 1.8 + 2 = 3.8 m and 705 kg, every number of it calculated in the derivations

critic.weak_point: 705 kg assumes the shape never changes, but the film's own fact shows real giants stay thinner (Wadlow: 199 kg at 2.72 m, where the cube gives 258 kg)
critic.fix: the assumption is spoken (step 8: everything grew in proportion), the caption says '705 kg if the shape holds', the counter's second label says it too, and reality step 9 gives the real Wadlow figure next to it

critic.weak_point: The plan had you walking at 705 kg while the reality text said the skeleton fails - the two fought each other
critic.fix: the load per square centimetre doubles, so the skeleton itself still holds (static bone stress stays well under the fracture limit) while the joints, the muscles and the heart run out first; the figure now stands still beside the fountain instead of walking

critic.weak_point: 'Your shadow covers the whole market by noon' was backwards - noon gives the shortest shadow of the day, about 2 m for a 3.8 m body
critic.fix: the shadow claim is gone; step 10 now says the market goes on around your legs, which is true at any hour

critic.weak_point: The counter freezes at the climax while the last line says the growth has not stopped, and the plan only explained that in the reality text, which nobody sees
critic.fix: the counter's own labels now say it: 'HEIGHT · FIRST 8 YEARS' and 'MASS · SAME SHAPE', short enough for a phone, so the frozen number is the eight-year window

critic.weak_point: Step 5 said a cart reaches your knee, but the counter runs 5 s per year, so at that moment you are 2.25 m and the cart reaches your thigh
critic.fix: the line now says the thigh; the same sum says the door frame is at your chest in step 7, which is where that shot puts it

critic.weak_point: Step 6 said the tallest man never stopped growing, which the source does not say
critic.fix: step 6 and the facts now carry what the source really gives - 2.72 m and 199 kg

critic.weak_point: The reality text said a 705 kg body needs nine times the food, simply copying the ninefold weight - but metabolism follows mass to the power 0.75, so the real figure is about five times
critic.fix: reality step 9 now says about five times the food, roughly thirteen thousand kilocalories a day, with the 0.75 exponent given

questions.question: How do we show 'you' - with the camera standing where you stand, or with a figure that grows on screen?
questions.my_choice: a figure that grows: the story IS the body, so we scale one Kenney character from x1 to x2.11, keep everyone else at normal size for the metre scale, and let it stand still beside the fountain at the end

questions.question: The place: reuse old-town (already built) or build the 'giant human world' of PLAN-100 #72 (still to build)?
questions.my_choice: old-town: it is ready, and its doors (2 m), stalls, cart, fountain and 3.2 m lanterns give exactly the metre scale this story needs

questions.question: The one new thing: the growing figure and its scale animation in code (no new model files, no new licences)
questions.my_choice: yes, one new thing in code: the figure is a scaled Kenney mini-character, everything else comes from environments/old-town.js
